full_stack_ascent.note: Mach < 1 and margin >= 1.5 cal both satisfied. Separation occurs at t=2.5s, well before first apogee (t~10.5s for the dropped booster branch, t~211s for the sustainer branch) -- genuine staging confirmed.

free_descent_unpowered_reference.note: 56.1 m/s matches the '~58 m/s' figure the directive attributes to the current Phase 4B campaign almost exactly -- strong evidence Phase 4B is observing the SAME underlying unpowered-descent physics for this topology family, just without finding the narrow legal delay window documented below.

powered_result_at_literal_historical_del.delay_reference: absolute mission time from LAUNCH (t=0); confirmed from the generated ORK XML: the retro motor's <ignitionevent>launch</ignitionevent> with <ignitiondelay>{s1_retro_delay}</ignitiondelay>, i.e. retro ignition is scheduled at t = 0 + s1_retro_delay seconds
warnings: RETRO MOTOR NEVER IGNITES BEFORE GROUND CONTACT. The booster's natural (unpowered) ground-hit time for this candidate is t=30.342s. A retro ignition scheduled at t=33.104s is 2.76s AFTER the vehicle has already reached the ground. retro_burn_diagnostics.sample_count=0 -- the OpenRocket simulation terminates at GROUND_HIT before the retro motor's ignition event ever fires. The powered result is bit-identical (to 13 significant figures) to the unpowered free-descent reference above.

Confirmed across the directive-specified +/-0.02s robustness window (33.084/33.094/33.104/33.114/33.124s): all five delays produce touchdown_total_speed_ms=56.13895535481251 with retro_sample_count=0 (see phase4c-literal-33p104-robustness.json).

powered_result_at_corrected_delay.delay_reference: absolute mission time from LAUNCH (t=0), same convention as above
powered_result_at_corrected_delay.how_found: Coarse-to-fine bisection sweep of s1_retro_delay in [25.0, 33.104]s through the same authority path (phase4c-delay-sweep-diagnostic.json -> -fine.json -> -fine2.json -> -finest.json). Touchdown speed falls from ~50 m/s at 25.0s to a sharp local minimum near 29.86s, then rises sharply back toward the 56.1 m/s free-fall value once ignition is scheduled past the natural ground-hit time (t=30.34s unpowered), with a non-monotonic dip-rise-dip pattern at the 2 ms grid immediately around the minimum (29.858:5.372, 29.860:4.907, 29.862:3.827, 29.864:3.589, 29.866:6.144, 29.868:5.127 m/s -- see phase4c-delay-sweep-finest.json). CORRECTED 2026-07-20 (phase5a): only 29.862s and 29.864s are confirmed legal on this grid; this is NOT a continuous 29.862-29.868s legal interval. A screen or search algorithm sampling coarser than ~1ms can still easily miss the whole basin.
powered_result_at_corrected_delay.velocity_at_ignition_enu: not directly logged by run_sim(); retro_burn_diagnostic.peak_thrust_sample (t=30.248s, mid-burn) reports vx=3.113, vy=4.876, vz=-33.445 m/s in OpenRocket's East/North/vertical world frame
powered_result_at_corrected_delay.note_on_fraction_fields: osifog_sweep._retro_burn_diagnostic() reports fraction_opposing_velocity=1.0 and fraction_vertical_braking=1.0 for all 111 post-ignition thrust samples -- every single sample opposes both total and vertical velocity. This is the 'verified opposing thrust' qualifier from handoff.md, reproduced exactly.
powered_result_at_corrected_delay.motor_burning_at_contact_detail: H180W nominal burnout would be at t=31.177s (ignition 29.864 + burn_duration 1.313), but GROUND_HIT occurs at t=30.787s, 0.39s before nominal burnout -- the motor is still actively thrusting at touchdown.
warnings: This delay (29.864s) is NOT the literally-claimed historical value (33.104s) -- it is 3.240s earlier. It was found by an independent bisection search on the CURRENT pipeline, not copied from any historical artifact.

The touchdown speed (3.589 m/s) is close to but not exactly equal to the historically claimed 3.5135 m/s (delta = 0.076 m/s, 2.2% relative). Given the razor-thin (~2ms) legal window and its extreme sensitivity to delay (dTouchdownSpeed/dDelay ~ -1.6 m/s per ms in this region), a 0.076 m/s difference corresponds to roughly 0.05ms of delay precision or a very small difference in the exact source candidate's s0/nose_mass parameters (which the directive's own yaml clue did not exactly match -- see historical-3p5135-candidate.json unrecoverable_fields).

reproducibility_after_save_reopen.procedure: save_simulated_ork() executed the sim once and wrote the ZIP .ork with anti-tumble validated; the file was then reopened fresh (_load_ork_doc), the single saved simulation re-run with the same seed and the anti-tumble listener re-attached, and the GROUND_HIT event re-interpolated from the freshly simulated branch data.
